title: Congratulating and Giving Good Wishes
summary: Congratulating, wishing well, and reacting in celebration contexts.
whyItMatters: Good wishes are short but socially important. Choosing a phrase that matches the occasion, adding a personal detail, and responding warmly makes celebration language feel natural rather than memorized.

mentalModel.title: Match phrase to occasion
mentalModel.content: Birthday, wedding, holiday, exam, recovery, and journey wishes use different conventional phrases.

mentalModel.title: Add one personal line
mentalModel.content: After the standard wish, mention health, happiness, success, enjoyment, or a shared plan.

mentalModel.title: Receive the wish actively
mentalModel.content: Thank the person and, when natural, respond to the personal detail or include them in the celebration.

ruleBlocks.title: Choose the conventional opening
ruleBlocks.content: Use 'Alles Gute zum Geburtstag', 'Herzlichen Glückwunsch', 'Frohe Weihnachten', or another occasion-specific phrase.

ruleBlocks.title: Add a personal wish
ruleBlocks.content: Continue with 'Ich wünsche dir/Ihnen ...' plus Gesundheit, Glück, Erfolg, or a good experience.

ruleBlocks.title: Keep address consistent
ruleBlocks.content: Use 'dir/dein' informally and 'Ihnen/Ihr' formally throughout the message.

ruleBlocks.title: Thank and acknowledge
ruleBlocks.content: Respond with 'Vielen Dank', 'Das ist lieb/nett von dir/Ihnen', or a short relevant reply.

tables.title: Responding to Good Wishes
rows: Danke, das ist lieb von dir.
Vielen Dank, das ist sehr nett von Ihnen.
Danke! Komm doch später zur Feier.

sentenceStructure: Use 'zu' plus the appropriate article form for many occasions.
Respond with thanks and consistent register.

concepts: adapt tone to formal and personal contexts

comparisons.summary: The theme lesson supplies the occasions, dates, invitations, and customs that frame each wish.
Short hospitable instructions often surround a celebration exchange: 'Komm rein', 'Nimm dir Kuchen', or 'Feiern Sie schön'.

examples.de: A: Alles Gute zum Geburtstag! Ich wünsche dir viel Glück und Gesundheit. B: Danke, das ist lieb von dir.
examples.en: A: Happy birthday! I wish you lots of happiness and health. B: Thank you, that is kind of you.

examples.de: Herzlichen Glückwunsch zur Hochzeit! Alles Gute für eure gemeinsame Zukunft.
examples.en: Congratulations on your wedding! All the best for your future together.

examples.de: A: Frohe Weihnachten! B: Danke, gleichfalls!
examples.en: A: Merry Christmas! B: Thank you, same to you!

examples.de: Gute Besserung! Ich hoffe, du bist bald wieder gesund.
examples.en: Get well soon! I hope you are healthy again soon.

examples.de: Viel Erfolg bei der Prüfung! Du schaffst das.
examples.en: Good luck with the exam! You can do it.

commonMistakes.wrong: Use 'Alles Gute zum Geburtstag' for every occasion.
commonMistakes.correct: Choose a wish that matches the event.

commonMistakes.wrong: Ich wünsche Ihnen viel Glück für deine Zukunft.
commonMistakes.correct: Ich wünsche Ihnen viel Glück für Ihre Zukunft.

commonMistakes.wrong: Receive a personal wish with silence or an unrelated response.
commonMistakes.correct: Acknowledge it with thanks and, if appropriate, a reciprocal wish.
commonMistakes.reason: The response completes the social exchange.

specialCases: 'Gleichfalls' works when the same wish logically applies to both people.
'Herzlichen Glückwunsch' is used for achievements and milestones, not ordinary holidays.
Condolence language is distinct from congratulations and belongs to a later, more sensitive context.
tips: Build a phrase card for each occasion.
Add one genuine personal wish to every standard formula.
Practice both giving and receiving the message.
